description: After Codex restart, live cstar-kernel MCP is connected and root cstar_handoff works, but codex app-server proxy, app-server daemon version, mcpServerStatus/list, and config/read all select /home/morderith/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock and fail ENOENT; recover the supported direct app-server path that previously accepted config/mcpServer/reload without mutation.

statement: H1: the current codex app-server CLI is a legacy or optional-daemon client that hard-selects app-server-control.sock, while the earlier successful config/mcpServer/reload used a separate supported direct app-server protocol path; help and installed-source inspection should expose the distinction.

observations: H1 supported: codex app-server help explicitly describes app-server proxy as a client for the running app-server control socket and exposes --sock; daemon version is a local managed-daemon query. The top-level app-server command is a separate server with stdio:// default or explicit unix/ws listen endpoints. Installed codex is a Node launcher over a native static binary; binary strings contain both control-socket diagnostics and in-process app-server channel diagnostics. This explains why current CLI probes choose the optional daemon socket but does not yet recover the earlier direct host request.

statement: H2: the earlier successful config/mcpServer/reload was sent through the Codex host's embedded app-server JSON-RPC channel, not through codex app-server proxy; local session/rollout/receipt text should reveal the exact supported direct client invocation or API.

observations: H2 supported by session evidence: the prior accepted reload was a raw JSON-RPC app-server protocol request with method config/mcpServer/reload and params null, written as one newline-delimited message to the verified Desktop app-server stdio input after checking its command line contained app-server --analytics-default-enabled. The request returned the recorded accepted/queued result; no codex app-server proxy or daemon socket was involved.

statement: H3: app-server-control.sock belongs only to the managed local app-server daemon/remote-control tooling; the active Codex Desktop app-server is stdio:// and therefore should not create or listen on that socket. Current command lines, fd topology, socket listing, and bounded config-key inspection should confirm this and identify whether a safe read-only request path exists.

observations: H3 supported: current Codex Desktop app-server is a node wrapper plus native child, both running app-server --analytics-default-enabled with identical stdin/stdout pipes and no listening UNIX/TCP endpoint. The managed-daemon commands independently hard-select /home/morderith/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock, which is absent; bounded config-key inspection found no app-server/daemon/socket/listen override. The control socket is not expected for this embedded stdio app-server.

statement: H4: a direct read-only mcpServerStatus/list request cannot be safely issued from this shell through the recovered stdio path because stdin/stdout are the live Desktop app-server channel; doing so would require host mediation or the same process-fd injection used for mutation. Therefore the minimal safe next action is the already-authorized host-mediated cstar-kernel reload, not a new socket or broad restart.

observations: H4: no separate safe read-only client is exposed by the installed CLI. codex app-server proxy and daemon version both fail before protocol exchange on the absent managed-daemon socket. The only recovered live channel is the shared embedded app-server stdio pipe; injecting mcpServerStatus/list there from this shell would be the same host-level fd intervention prohibited by this read-only debug assignment and could consume Desktop protocol traffic, so no status request was sent.
